digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III, V, VI and ch. 4–5

teaser.en: The 'black mlala', told apart from its relatives by the darkness of its bark.

summary.en: Mlala mwiru is an ebony-family tree of the coastal forests of Kenya and Tanzania, named for its dark bark.

about.en: *Mlala mwiru* is a tree of the ebony family, *Diospyros*. Like its relatives it has simple, alternate, leathery leaves, small bell-shaped flowers and round fruits held in a persistent calyx. Pakia's informants identified it by its leaves, and its name comes from its comparatively dark bark.

where.en: It is native to south-eastern Kenya and Tanzania, in the dry coastal forests.

culture.en: Stem colour is one of the ways Digo speakers tell apart plants they see as related. Pakia sets *mlala mwiru* against *mlala mwereru* (*Monodora grandidieri*), which is the white form.

names.en: *Mlala mwiru* means 'black *mlala*', the black form of *mlala* (Pakia gives *mlala* as *Diospyros greenwayi*) because its bark is darker. At one point in his main text Pakia glosses the name as 'white mlala', which seems to be a slip, because his name notes and the colour words agree it is black (*mwiru*). The Mgombato dictionary gives *mlala* only as raffia, which is a different plant. There is no English or Swahili name in the sources.
